sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster, at 5.8% a year, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F20][F28].
FY2020 was the trough: revenue fell 4.5% and operating income 19.9% on coal-ash settlement charges and pandemic-driven volume losses [D155][D156][P60].
FY2022 was the step change, with revenue up 17.1% on rate cases, favorable weather and higher volumes [D239][P26][P33].
FY2024 net income rose 59.2% largely because the prior year carried impairments on the Commercial Renewables sale [D320][P18].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and 3.6pp of its 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest customer class at 43.3% of revenue, contributing 2.8pp of FY2025 growth [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp of FY2025 growth, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% [D566][D682].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 41.4% [D359][D358][D378].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% a year against 9.7% net income growth, as the diluted share count rose from 691 million to 777 million [F202][F200][X106][X115].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, 4.3pp above the 22.9% median and 7.5pp above the FY2020 low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
The FY2025 margin rose 0.8pp as revenue growth outpaced operating-cost growth by only 0.3pp [D370][D379].
D&A reached 24.3% of revenue in FY2025, up from 21.4% in FY2024 [D341][D303].
Net margin of 15.7% sits 11.5pp below operating margin, reflecting interest expense of $3.6 billion and an 11.2% effective tax rate [F47][D967][X63][D345].
Net margin ranks at the 25th peer percentile against a 17.6% median, while operating margin ranks at the 75th [D951][D952][D949].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, near the 2.59x window median [F77][F38][D346][D958].
Free cash flow was negative $1.69 billion, a -5.3% margin, against a -5.8% window median [F97][D343][D939].
Capex of $14.0 billion was 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A [F87][D342][D348].
FY2022 conversion fell to 2.32x as rising fuel costs drove undercollections that increased borrowings [D226][P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, equal to 282.3% of revenue, with cash of just $245 million [D352][D353][F137].
That net-debt ratio is worse than the 235.4% peer median, ranking at the 33rd percentile of three peers [D969][D968].
Total debt grew 6.6% in FY2025, with $11.9 billion issued against $5.7 billion repaid [D376][X133][X143].
Return on average equity of 9.7% trails the 12.6% peer median at the 0th percentile [D357][D956][D955].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x in FY2025, the window low, from 0.67x [F177][D943][F176].
Cash covers only 0.1 years of the latest free-cash-flow burn [D356].
Net debt has risen nine consecutive years, from $50.0 billion in FY2016 to $89.6 billion in FY2025 [D14][D352][R3].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [D269][D309][D347][R4].
FY2021 operating expenses, pretax income and tax were later restated, so FY2021 comparisons use first-reported values [X29][X69][X79][R6].
If FY2026 operating margin holds above the 22.9% window median, the margin expansion trend is intact; a drop toward the 19.7% low would reverse it [D933][D931].
Watch free cash flow against the -5.8% window median; a return to the FY2024 0.2% high would signal capex relief [D939][D938].
Watch the current ratio against the 0.55x FY2025 level; a further decline below the 0.53x window low would tighten liquidity [F177][D943].
